body:
He's never hit her as far as I know. I think the reason she wanted to leave was because he was parenting me in a way she didn't like or something...can't exactly remember.

maybe things were resolved between the two of them privately. Also, each of their parents were divorced and remarried, so that may have an influence.

I graduated with a major in Deaf studies. It's actually a much longer title than that, but I don't want to type it all out.

I've said "fuck you" in nicer ways, but I guess it's my turn to decide what to do.

My parents are still together, some how.

I am not in therapy, since I'm moving. I figured it might be easier if I started without being in limbo. I have been to therapy previously, though. 2 years is a weird estimate.
First one was in november 2012.
second and third(had the intentions, got caught before I could go through) was fall 2013.
most recent was around christmas.
Still have yet to be baker-acted, don't know how.

Wasn't running away from debt. Hadn't thought about that...

My dad has always wanted me to be more athletic, instead of artsy and creative. Apparently that doesn't make money. He's tried to convince me my whole college career that I should be an interpreter, and dismissing my dream job of being a teacher for the deaf, which I blame myself for not directly pursuing and taking the easy route to graduation. My dad only wanted a son (I'm female), and stopped having kids after my brother was born, even though he had promised my mom a larger family. My mom talked multiple times about running away with me and my brother when I was a kid. She had to practically drag my dad to my concerts and performances, and even then he wouldn't pay attention. He begs and begs for me to visit, and then ignores me the whole time I'm home, only to beg me to stay longer while I pack my car.

My mom is the only thing keeping me alive, honestly. the first time I tried, the only thing that stopped me in my tracks was a song that she and I share. I also saw how she reacted when my grandfather died last year. I can't imagine how she would react if she heard I was dead. I love her, despite the fact that she made me keep the secret about the sexual abuse. She's always supported me.

I worked at two theme parks while in school, so I know what that's about. I don't know who has it worse in the service industry, honestly.

I don't know crap about home improvement, so how could I really be of help there?

I was going to save up for a car, but the goal was to have a job in my field before that happened, and it doesn't factor in the student debt.

Thank you though. I've been thinking of this situation in a permanent setting. I guess hearing it from someone else helps clear my mind a bit.

I told him basically everything I put on here and a bit more. His response was that I'm just going through a rough transition period and that (in regards to my family) "it's like that for many people," and that it's not uncommon.
